official.deadline_note: No single closing date: the official page states 'This scholarship is for all areas of study and is reviewed monthly. The above closing date does not apply.' Offshore applicants must apply by 30 November for A trimester, 31 May for B trimester, 31 August for C trimester and 31 October for H or X trimester offers of place; applications received within four weeks of the start of A, B, C or H trimester are not considered.
official.application_cycle: Continuous intake reviewed monthly; 2026 regulations in force
official.status_note: The official scholarship page is marked 'Accepting applications'.
official.tuition_coverage_note: 'The scholarships are tuition fees credits paid in NZD, have a value of up to $15,000 for undergraduate study and up to $10,000 for postgraduate study.' 'The total value offered is a contribution towards tuition fees only, and all remaining tuition fees and other costs must be met through other means.'
official.funding_period: one-off, paid in first trimester of study
benefits: Up to NZD$15,000 towards tuition fees (up to $15,000 undergraduate, up to $10,000 postgraduate)
Open to all areas of study
Paid in full in the first trimester of study
Successful applicants may be called upon to become global ambassadors for the University of Waikato

Have received a conditional or unconditional offer of place from the University of Waikato
Have a minimum GPA equivalency of B+ in the qualification used to gain entrance to the University of Waikato
Not be eligible for one of the Vice-Chancellor's International Excellence Scholarships for specific countries or regions
Not be currently enrolled in the University of Waikato College or any University of Waikato degree programme
requirements: Read the scholarship regulations before commencing the application process
Complete an application to enrol at the University of Waikato first, in order to gain MyWaikato access
Upload a conditional or unconditional Offer of Place as part of the online submission
Provide specific details on why you want to study at the University of Waikato and how you will be a global ambassador for the University
Enrol within 12 months of the start date indicated in the Offer of Place, full-time (at least 120 points)
Reside in New Zealand and maintain international fee-paying status for the entire tenure
documents: Conditional or unconditional Offer of Place from the University of Waikato, uploaded with the online scholarship submission
Statement in the application giving specific details on why you want to study at the University of Waikato and how you will be a global ambassador
Academic records evidencing the B+ GPA equivalency in the entrance qualification
Completed University of Waikato application to enrol (prerequisite for MyWaikato scholarship access)
selection_criteria: Potential to become global ambassadors for the University of Waikato
coverage: Tuition fees only: 'The total value offered is a contribution towards tuition fees only, and all remaining tuition fees and other costs must be met through other means.'

Log in to MyWaikato and open the 'Scholarships' tab
Select the Vice-Chancellor's International Excellence Scholarship and submit with the Offer of Place upload and ambassadorial statement
official.application_route: Apply online via MyWaikato ('Scholarships' tab) after first completing an application to enrol

official.citizenship_residency: Open to new international students; recipients must reside in New Zealand for the entire tenure and maintain international fee-paying status

official.duration: 12-month tenure, with the full value paid in the first trimester of study
official.description: Established in 2015 (prior to 2023 named the University of Waikato International Excellence Scholarship) to promote educational opportunities, foster internationalisation and support talented international applicants enrolling for the first time into undergraduate or postgraduate programmes at the University of Waikato, this scholarship provides a tuition-fee credit of up to NZD$15,000.
official.program_type: University international excellence scholarship (tuition fee credit)

not_confirmed: english_requirement - no English-language requirement is published for this scholarship (programme admission requirements apply separately)

applicant_utility.summary: This Waikato award gives new international students a tuition credit of up to NZD$15,000 (up to $10,000 for postgraduate study), decided on academic merit plus ambassadorial potential in monthly rounds rather than one annual deadline. You must hold a Waikato Offer of Place before you can even submit, so the enrolment application is genuinely step one. Everything beyond tuition - living costs, insurance, flights - remains your own responsibility.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-performing international school or university leavers (B+ equivalency) starting a full-time undergraduate or taught postgraduate programme at Waikato for the first time.
application_readiness_checklist: Apply to enrol at Waikato first and obtain a conditional or unconditional Offer of Place - the scholarship application sits behind it in MyWaikato
Prepare academic records that evidence the B+ GPA equivalency used for entrance
Draft the ambassadorial statement with specific reasons for choosing Waikato and concrete ambassador ideas, since it is a scored selection factor
Screen yourself against the exclusion list before applying (limited-place programmes, postgraduate teaching programmes, sponsored or exchange students, prior Waikato enrolment)
Submit ahead of your trimester cut-off (30 Nov A / 31 May B / 31 Aug C / 31 Oct H-X) and never within four weeks of a trimester start
common_rejection_risks: Applying for a limited-entry programme (e.g. Master of Nursing Practice) or a postgraduate teaching programme (e.g. Master of Teaching and Learning), which the regulations expressly exclude
Having already paid tuition fees or lodged a student visa application at the time of application - either makes you ineligible
Offshore applicants who apply after the cut-off for their trimester of entry
Holding another Waikato-funded tuition scholarship, an Education New Zealand scholarship or a Manaaki Scholarship, which cannot be held concurrently
A generic ambassadorial statement - selection weighs global-ambassador potential alongside academic merit
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Accommodation, food, transport and other living costs; any tuition above the credit; health insurance; and flights to New Zealand - the award applies to tuition fees only.
document_audit: The Offer of Place upload is mandatory in the online submission; without it the application cannot be assessed
Academic records must substantiate the B+ equivalency in the qualification used to gain entrance, not just overall performance
The ambassadorial statement must give specific detail - the regulations call for specifics on why Waikato and how you would act as a global ambassador, so boilerplate text works against you
alerts: Scholarship offers lapse if not accepted within 14 days, and the offer is valid only for 12 months from the start date in the Offer of Place unless deferral is approved
Withdrawing after one trimester causes the pro-rated scholarship value to be removed from your account
The award requires full-time enrolment (at least 120 points) and continued international fee-paying status; any change in status can reduce or remove the scholarship
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Enrolment application -> Offer of Place issued -> MyWaikato Scholarships tab application with offer upload and statement -> panel decision normally within 3-4 weeks -> 14-day window to accept the scholarship offer.

official.deadline_note: The official page publishes applicant-type windows rather than one date: opening 1 May in the year prior to study for offshore students and 1 July for onshore students; closing 10 December for a semester 1 (February) start, 30 April for a semester 2 (July) start for offshore students, and 15 August for onshore students. The 10 December 2026 date is the next closing date in the current offshore cycle for a February 2027 start; the page states day and month without a year.
official.application_cycle: Annual cycle - offshore applications open 1 May in the year prior to study; onshore Entrance Scholarship applications 1 July to 15 August
official.status_note: The official page publishes recurring windows rather than a live status: opens 1 May in the year prior to study for offshore students and 1 July for onshore students, closing 10 December (semester 1 start), 30 April (semester 2 start, offshore) and 15 August (onshore).
official.tuition_coverage_note: 'Payment of the scholarship will be made as a credit towards tuition fees only.'
benefits: Payable only as a credit towards tuition fees
Semester 2 (July) starters are eligible: half ($5,000) is released as a tuition credit in semester 2, with the balance released in semester 1 of the following year
No separate scholarship application for offshore applicants - automatically assessed during the admission process
eligibility: Be an international student who has completed secondary (high) school, or study at another approved institution that grants University Entrance, either overseas or within New Zealand

Be intending to enrol, or already enrolled, in full-time undergraduate degree-level study, or in an approved foundation diploma programme with the objective of progressing into an undergraduate degree
Intend to study at the University of Otago from 100-level (first year) through to degree attainment
Study on campus throughout the duration of your studies
Not be enrolling in a foundation certificate programme (foundation certificate enrollees are ineligible)
Not be sponsored by your home government or the New Zealand government
requirements: Onshore applicants (secondary or foundation study completed in New Zealand): submit the online Entrance Scholarship application and complete the first stages of enrolment through eVision during the 1 July to 15 August application period
Offshore applicants: agree in your eVision study application that you would like to be considered for international scholarships
Hold entrance to the University of Otago and admission to a degree-level programme of study
Be enrolled and studying full-time (0.9 or more EFTS), full-year, at degree level
documents: eVision study application with agreement to be considered for international scholarships (offshore route)

Online Entrance Scholarship application with the compulsory Education section (onshore route): education system(s) studied in and candidate number, IB programme teacher contact details, and any issues affecting Year 12 results
Academic transcript - received automatically by the University, so listed achievements must go beyond it

Optional section statements with named referees where relevant: leadership (3 examples, max 200 characters each), academic achievement, sport/cultural, extra-curricular, financial or family circumstances, disability, Maori or Pacific involvement (up to 1,500 characters each)
selection_criteria: Academic potential, as demonstrated by programme admission
coverage: Tuition fees only: the scholarship is 'payable only as a credit towards tuition fees'
application_method: Offshore: agree to scholarship consideration in the eVision study application - assessment is automatic during admission, with no separate scholarship form
Onshore: complete the first stages of eVision enrolment, then apply through the online Entrance Scholarship application between 1 July and 15 August
Actively accept the scholarship offer by the deadline in the offer letter, in addition to accepting the admission offer
official.application_route: Offshore: tick scholarship consideration in your eVision study application; onshore: apply via the online Entrance Scholarship application (1 July - 15 August)
official.study_mode: Full-time (0.9 or more EFTS), full-year, degree-level undergraduate study, on campus throughout
official.citizenship_residency: Open to international students, including those who completed secondary school overseas or in New Zealand; government-sponsored students are not eligible, and a change from international to domestic residency during tenure may suspend or terminate the award
official.description: Established in 2020, the Vice-Chancellor's Scholarship for International Students celebrates and welcomes international students to the University of Otago | Ōtākou Whakaihu Waka as valued members of the University community and is awarded to support students to pursue their academic goals; it is an Entrance Scholarship worth NZD$10,000 payable only as a credit towards tuition fees.
official.program_type: University international entrance scholarship (tuition fee credit)

not_confirmed: english_requirement - no English-language requirement is published for this scholarship (programme admission requirements apply separately)
deadline year - the official page gives day/month windows (10 December, 30 April, 15 August) without stating a year
verification.notes: Value (NZD$10,000), one-year tenure, tuition-credit-only payment, semester-2 split payment, single-award rule, government-sponsor exclusion, application routes and opening/closing windows verified on the official scholarship page, the VCSIS regulations PDF, the international scholarships page and the Undergraduate Entrance Scholarship terms and conditions on otago.ac.nz.

applicant_utility.summary: Otago pays NZD$10,000 as a tuition-fee credit over one year to new international students starting full-time on-campus undergraduate study, selected on academic potential as demonstrated by programme admission. Most offshore applicants are assessed automatically during admission with no separate scholarship form, so the effective deadline is the admission application window - 1 May to 10 December for a February start. Students who finished secondary school in New Zealand instead join the Entrance Scholarship round that runs 1 July to 15 August.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International secondary-school leavers (or approved foundation diploma completers) with a confirmed place in full-time first-year undergraduate study at Otago.
application_readiness_checklist: Offshore: lodge your eVision study application early in the window and confirm you have agreed to be considered for international scholarships
Onshore: start eVision enrolment, then submit the Entrance Scholarship application between 1 July and 15 August
Check your Offer of Place enrolment date works for you - the scholarship lapses if you cannot commence and deferral is not possible
Confirm you are not government-sponsored (home or New Zealand government) and are not entering a foundation certificate programme
Watch for the offer letter after acceptance and actively accept by its deadline
common_rejection_risks: Being sponsored by a home government or the New Zealand government, which the regulations expressly exclude
Confusing a foundation certificate programme (ineligible) with an approved foundation diploma progressing to a degree (eligible)
Assuming multiple applications or Offers of Place stack - the scholarship is only ever formally awarded once
Missing the window for your applicant type and start semester (10 December or 30 April offshore; 15 August onshore)
Holding another Otago Undergraduate Entrance Scholarship - only the highest-value award is normally received
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Dunedin living and accommodation costs, insurance, travel, and any tuition above the $10,000 credit - the award is a tuition credit only.
document_audit: For the Entrance Scholarship application the Education section is compulsory; the University receives your transcript automatically, so statements must add information beyond it
Optional leadership, sport/cultural and extra-curricular sections each require short statements plus named referees - only complete sections you can evidence
A declaration must be accepted before the application can be submitted
alerts: Semester 2 (July) starters receive $5,000 in semester 2 with the balance released in semester 1 of the following year - plan your cash flow around the split
A change from international to domestic residency during tenure can suspend or terminate the scholarship and trigger part or full repayment
Withdrawal or stopping study cancels entitlement, and the University may require repayment of funds already paid
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: eVision study application with scholarship consent (offshore) or Entrance Scholarship application 1 July - 15 August (onshore) -> automatic assessment during admission -> scholarship offer letter with an acceptance deadline -> tuition credit applied.
